stops.title: Faraday's laws & Lenz's law
stops.inShort: Faraday's laws: (1) Changing magnetic flux induces an emf; (2) Magnitude |e| = dΦ_B/dt. Lenz's law: direction of induced current opposes the cause producing it (conservation of energy): e = −N dΦ_B/dt.

stops.title: Motional emf & eddy currents
stops.inShort: Translational motional emf in rod of length l moving at v perpendicular to B: e = B l v. Rotational emf in rod of length l rotating with ω about one end: e = ½ B ω l². Eddy currents are circulating currents induced in bulk conductors.

stops.title: Self-inductance, mutual inductance & energy density
stops.inShort: Self-inductance L: Φ = L I, e = −L dI/dt. Energy stored U = ½ L I²; energy density u_B = B²/(2μ₀). Mutual inductance M = k √(L₁ L₂), e₂ = −M dI₁/dt.

stops.title: Transformer
stops.inShort: Works on mutual induction for AC only. Transformer equation: E_s / E_p = N_s / N_p = I_p / I_s (ideal). Step-up: N_s > N_p; Step-down: N_s < N_p.

items.f: e = B l v,  e_rot = (1/2) B ω l²
items.s: For rod rotating about one end in perpendicular B.

board.text: A transformer increases an alternating e.m.f. from 220 V to 880 V. If primary coil has 1000 turns, the number of turns in the secondary coil are ____.

board.answer: Self-inductance (L) of a coil is defined as the magnetic flux linked with the coil per unit current flowing through it (L = Φ/I), or numerically equal to the emf induced in the coil per unit rate of change of current (|e| = L |dI/dt|).

board.text: Two coils having self inductances 60 mH each are coupled with each other. If the coefficient of coupling is 0.75, calculate the mutual inductance between them.

A conducting bar is rotating with constant angular speed around a pivot at one end in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its plane of rotation. Obtain an expression for the rotational e.m.f. induced between the ends of the bar.
board.answer:
Consider a conducting rod of length l rotating with constant angular speed ω in uniform perpendicular magnetic field B.
Take a small element dr at distance r from the pivot. Its linear speed is v = ω r.
Small emf induced across dr: de = B v dr = B ω r dr.
Integrating from r = 0 to r = l:
e = ∫(0 to l) B ω r dr = B ω [r²/2](0 to l) = ½ B ω l².

points.text: Small element dr with v = ωr and de = Bωr dr
Final expression e = ½ B ω l²

board.text: Explain why the equivalent inductance of two coils connected in parallel is less than the inductance of either of the coils.
board.answer:
When two coils L₁ and L₂ (far apart, M = 0) are connected in parallel across a changing source, the same induced emf e acts across both: I = I₁ + I₂ ⇒ dI/dt = dI₁/dt + dI₂/dt.
Since |e| = L_p (dI/dt) = L₁(dI₁/dt) = L₂(dI₂/dt), we get 1/L_p = 1/L₁ + 1/L₂.
Because 1/L_p > 1/L₁ and 1/L_p > 1/L₂, L_p is smaller than both L₁ and L₂.

points.text: Same induced emf and I = I₁ + I₂ giving 1/L_p = 1/L₁ + 1/L₂
Conclusion that L_p < L₁ and L_p < L₂
